utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I see two standing. I think you were first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And now it's just one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I was just pouring a glass of water. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Before the witness is brought in, we just have a brief matter to raise. It's actually a point of agreement rather than disagreement, so it should only take a moment. It is a stipulation with respect to this witness which I hope will save some time, certainly on cross-examination. The stipulation is as follows. On April 7th of 2002, this witness, L-12, was interviewed by CCIU/UNMIK. On June 5th of 2002, the Albanian statement of the witness was read back to him. On this occasion, two photo spreads were shown to the witness, each containing six photographs. These photo spreads were prepared by CCIU/UNMIK and have been the subject of discussion in this courtroom before. But just to be clear that while the exact order of the photographs as they were shown to the witness is unknown, the identity of these six photographs in each photo spread is known and will be provided to the Court at some point. One of the photo spreads contained a photograph of the accused Isak Musliu, and the other photo spread contained a photograph of the accused Haradin Bala. The witness L-12 was unable to recognise anybody in either of the photo spreads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it no comment is called for in respect of that from the Defence benches? In that case, we will have the witness. We will move into private session for the initial stages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you a Kosovar Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention to the year 1998. In that year, did you support any political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about the LDK or Mr. Rugova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a supporter of Mr. Rugova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, in 1998 - and please don't name the village that you were living in - but in the area you were living in did you start to hear anything about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what you heard about the KLA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. Can you tell us what you heard about the KLA in 1998, in your area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UCK was there in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring and early summer of 1998, was there any fighting between the KLA and the Serbs in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- then is when it all started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when the fighting started? Did you have to leave your home, you and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we left our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went up in the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it you and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I left together with my family and went back home two days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again in the spring and summer of 1998, were you part of any army or police force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are now in open session. Your identity is still protected, but I would ask you to take care not to use your name, please. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll remind you to keep -- for the benefit of the interpreters to keep speaking up and speaking clearly into the microphone. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What happened is that they took -- drove us there and then Shala opened the door, took the sacks off our heads. Then they chained me with a cow chain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you chained with a cow chain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was inside the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't use the name of the -- your family member that was also there, but can you describe for us how you were chained.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tied us at the wood piece where they would tie the animals usually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was the chain connected to your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again without saying the name, were you chained to another person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the chain that tied the two of you connected to the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Shala. Did Shala do anything after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala beat me with a stick, with a heavy stick and said to me the words: You are a king.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want you to say the name of your village, but did he also -- when he said you are a king, did he also mention your village?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because he knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he beat you with a stick. Where did that beating occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He hit me on my ribs, on my head, on my hands, and also on my legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you still inside of the barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, inside the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long the beating lasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they beat me until I lost my consciousness, and I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "they" beat you. Was there other people beating you in addition to Shala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that moment they didn't beat us more. There was also Murrizi there, but I cannot tell whether he hit me or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Shala -- again, don't mention any names. But did Shala beat anybody else or did he just beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean he beat other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I can't tell after how much time, but I remember we were beaten during the night, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the moment I'm just talking about that first time when Shala beat you. Do you remember if he beat only you or did he also beat the person that you were chained with?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, at this time, Your Honour, I would object. The question has now been asked on a number of occasions. I believe that Mr. Whiting has received his answer and I would appreciate it if we could move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. I gather you are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can move on. I don't think the question was answered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness, again talking about that beating by Shala, how did you feel after that beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only after three days to four days this pain was relieved. They also beat us during the night. Shala had the keys from the barn. He knows who was beating me. He knows who took me somewhere. He knows everything what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how long were you kept in that barn in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Shala, how often did you see him at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he had the keys to the barn. Would he let people in and out of the barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He knew -- he knew who come inside the barn to beat us; he would put the people inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also see him at times during the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he bring food to you at times during the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Together with Murrizi sometime -- with that Murrizi that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Every day, every day Shala was there. He was the main person of that detention centre there. I didn't see anyone else there to open the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you -- I'm going to ask you to describe for us the barn that you were in. First of all, were there other people in the barn besides you and the person you were chained with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the room have a window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the window on the same wall as the door or a different wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you'd enter through those doors, the window was on the left. This was a small window, not a big one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand your answer that the window was on a different wall from the door? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door was right there, straight. The window was on the left, on the same wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same wall or a different wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the same wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other people that were in the room, were they chained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what -- Witness, you have some water there if you want to take a break to drink some water.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's all right. I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the floor of the barn you were in was made of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was blood there. There was dung, whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the floor made of? Was it wood? Concrete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a concrete floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the temperature in the room when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What can I say? It's like staying in manure. I didn't have any means to find out what the temperature was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it hot in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had to use the toilet, what did you do? Were you allowed to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was doing everything there. I would eat there, I would stay there, I would drink there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you got for food.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would bring whatever they could find to eat or drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Like what kinds of things were you given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would give us potatoes and bread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get food every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes they would bring some macaroni, sometimes some other time of food, whatever they could find.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get food every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not every day. Once every two days or once every three days, once every four days. So there were days when we wouldn't eat a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed out of the room to walk around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to the other prisoners in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not able to talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I couldn't. I couldn't -- not dare to talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you didn't dare? Did anybody tell you not to talk to the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think there comes a point in time when the leading really does need to stop. This has been going on for some period of time; intermittent questions are posed that are not leading. But for the most part Mr. Whiting is successfully testifying here, and I wish he would stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's a fair observation, Mr. Whiting. I think it's largely unconscious or I would have intervened myself earlier, but you do slip the answers in at times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I have tried to be careful, but I will try harder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what's called for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you did not dare talk to other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all I wasn't able because they did not allow me to speak. For some time I was not able to speak; I was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe your physical condition when you were in that room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was almost close to death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody ever tell you why you were being held in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No one told me anything, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you were given water.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They gave us plastic bottles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you the plastic bottles of water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we went there, we found the bottles there. There were filled bottles there; we found them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you what's an image from Exhibit P5. It's on your computer monitor. And you've seen this before, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask the case manager to pan us around. And, Witness, I would ask you for a moment to just look. And if we could go inside of the room. For the record, on Exhibit P6 it's room A4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Witness, do you recognise this room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it. It's the cowshed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask the -- you say it's the cowshed. Is this the -- have you been in this room before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they took me, they put me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the room you were held in for a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the case manager to pan around the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the window there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that how the window was when you were held in the room for one month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was exactly there. It was on the left side. When you enter the room, it was on the right side. I don't know how you can take it from left or right. That's the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the case manager could continue panning around the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I see it. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember where -- if the case manager could stop for a moment. Do you remember where in the room you were chained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the corner of the room, up there in the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the corner -- in one of the corners you can see right now on the image?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were two people who were taken there and I was on one side and the other one was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the case manager to zoom in on the chains that are there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is this the kind of chain that was used to chain you in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's a cow chain, chain used for the animals, to tie up animals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, are you certain that this is the room you were held in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure. I was in the front, somewhere in the front of the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you say "the front," were you in the part of the room that's near the door or the other part of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter the room, right there. That's where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We can take that image off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you ever taken out of that room, the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken out after some days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala took me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it during the day or at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He blindfolded me and he took me somewhere. He took me in the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how far away it was that he took you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was approximately 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got into that barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Rrahman Qerqizi was there and two other women. I'm not sure, probably because I have forgotten the names who was there, but his name was mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose name was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Qerqizi, Qerqizi's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was said in connection with Qerqizi's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala was there. Shala knows it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Witness, I'm asking you. Do you remember what was said about -- that had Qerqizi's name in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Qerqizi was mentioned. His sister mentioned, but I'm not sure about it. And my brother said, Qerqiz. And then they put me there and they beat me. But they mentioned the name of Alija there, where is Alija, they said. I said, The Serbs killed him, the Shkje killed him. They did not beat me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said his sister mentioned I believe the name "Qerqizi."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Qerqizi's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know it was his sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just -- I'm just saying what she said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did she say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The brother said. He called him "brother."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She called him "brother" and did she use the name Qerqizi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you were beaten by two men and two women. How do you know it was two men and two women? Because you said you were blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala beat me, and I saw it with the left part of my eye. And I saw that there were two men and two women. I saw it with the tail of my eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The translation that we got said that Shala beat you. Is -- did Shala beat you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Shala did not beat me there. Shala did not beat me there. There were four people who beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were able to see out of your blindfold that there were two men and two women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they put me down, they beat me. And I saw that there were two men and two women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the beating, please. How was the beating done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The women beat me and -- the women beat me. The men did not beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they use their hands or their feet or did they use weapons? What -- how was the beating done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me with fists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the beating in -- with anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me with fists and in my arm, and they hit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that they asked you about Ali.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me, Where is Ali? I told them that the Serbs killed him. And then they did not beat me anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break now for a rest until 5 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before the break you told us about a beating in a barn outside of the cowshed. And you told us that you heard the name Qerqiz. While you were at Lapusnik for one month, did you hear that name on any other occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know anything when I was inside. I was inside and I did not know what happened. They beat us, they beat us, whether it was Shala or someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the name Qerqiz, did you hear that again while you were at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard the name but I don't know who was the -- who the person was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you heard the name on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who was there. I don't know who the person was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how did you hear the name? Who said it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who mentioned the name because I was unable to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the name was mentioned by other prisoners or by people who came into the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who were in the cowshed mentioned the name, but I don't know who mentioned the name, who was inside the cowshed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about Shala. Could you describe -- could you describe for us, please, how Shala looked when you were at Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing black clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know approximately how old he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what to say, probably 56, 57 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know. He had moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe his skin, the colour of his skin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a brownish, brownish, dark brown complexion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he tall or short?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was tall -- neither tall nor short, medium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the build of his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was not very strongly built, rather thin I might say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left Lapusnik, did you ever see Shala again in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, have you seen the accused in this case on television before coming here to this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you to look around the courtroom, please. Look all around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to wait for my question. Do you see the man that you knew as Shala in the courtroom here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where he is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the first row or the second row?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He's in between the two men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can -- are you able to see what kind of tie he is wearing? Are you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot see his tie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I just need the record to be clear here, and I apologise. Can you just look once again and tell us if he is in the first row or is he in the second row. Do you understand that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In between, as you say it, in between the two ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're going to have to give me something more, Witness. Is he -- there are two rows. You're looking to the left. Is he in the row of men that's seated closer to you or the one that's closest to the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one closer to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the record reflect that the witness has identified the accused Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would interpose the same objection that I have with all other in-dock identifications made in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I already noted it with anticipation, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did there come a day when you were taken out of the cowshed and you left Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala took us out, got us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before Shala took you out, did something happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, something happened. A mine exploded there, a mine of the Serbs, a grenade, and then he took us out, the two of us. He let us go through the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When that happened, when you were taken out of the cowshed, how many other prisoners were in the cowshed with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. They were -- they left earlier. They gathered there, and I don't know -- I don't want to lie here. There were many. I cannot tell you the exact number. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were other prisoners in the cowshed on the day you were taken out. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were many other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Shala took you and the other prisoners out, where did he take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took us out and told us to go toward the forest and took us to Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask you to look at another image on the computer screen. And for the record, this is from Prosecution Exhibit 5 and it is image -- it is A8 in Exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit P6. Witness, do you see that image in front of you on the computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The doors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it? You say it's the doors, what doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The doors leading to the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the compound, did you go out of these doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if you went right or left when you walked out of those doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We left right, then we turned, and then we went toward the mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- by the way, Witness, you've told us you were in Lapusnik. How did you know you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I knew it was Lapusnik. I knew even when we went out toward the mountains, I knew it was Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you need to drink some water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it will get worse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were held for one month in this compound in Lapusnik, had you been to Lapusnik before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen every corner of Lapusnik, I've been everywhere in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times had you been to Lapusnik before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before going there? Well, there's no place in Lapusnik that I haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the cowshed before that day that you left Lapusnik, did you know then that you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they took me there and I got there, I didn't know that I was in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you realise that you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they took us out to the hills, then I realised it was Lapusnik. There couldn't have been any other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said when you left Lapusnik you went into the hills, the Berisa Mountains. Who --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the guards or the soldiers from Lapusnik with you when you went into the Berisa mountains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Murrizi was with us. Murrizi was his name, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other guards aside from Murrizi with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't seen any other guards, only the two of them were with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two of them, Murrizi and who else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe how you marched. Were you marching in a group? In a line? How did you march into the mountains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Shala and where was Murrizi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Murrizi was leading and then Shala came behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were any of the prisoners who were marching on this march injured, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A young man had his foot injured, but I don't know -- I don't know whether there were any other people who were injured. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The young man who had his foot injured, was he able to walk like the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was kept by others. He was helped by others. He was supported by -- whoever was able to support him helped him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, where did -- what happened when you went into the Berisa mountains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They put us into -- they led us into a kind of valley and they led us there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got into the valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They kept us for some time in the meadow we were taken into. And then the others were left there, and I don't know anything -- what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who released you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he do that? Could you describe that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They took us to a hill and then gave us a piece of paper and left them in Kazharek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was everybody released at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half of them were released; half were left there. I don't know then what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the piece of paper said on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not able to see it. (redacted)had that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- by the way, during the march before you were released, did you see anybody along the march?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were marching, we saw anyone [as interpreted], I was not able to see anyone. I don't know who was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I was released, I went to Kazharek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kazharek, some soldiers put us. And then when it got dusk then they gathered us again. They put us into a shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I should have asked you this. You said it got dusk. When you marched into the Berisa Mountains and were released, was it daytime or nighttime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was day, daytime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the shop that you mentioned, where was that, the shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kazharek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you -- were you still with the -- was the group that was released all together still at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they released us all together as a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after Kazharek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Kazharek they took us to Kubarac [phoen] -- Krajmirovce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get from Kazharek to Krajmirovce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I trekked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in Krajmirovce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They held that evening in Krajmirovce [as interpreted]. Then in the morning at dawn, they released us and let us go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody in your group that was released from Krajmirovce, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were released from Krajmirovce, do you -- are you able -- are you understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released from Krajmirovce, were you ever interviewed by the Serb authorities -- Serb police, Serb military -- about your time in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are in open session now and I'm going to ask you some more questions concerning this dispute, but I want you to be careful and not mention any names. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The dispute over this land began some months before the war started. True, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for purposes of our understanding, when do you say that the war started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war started -- now I can't really remember, but I believe this happened three to four months before the start of the war and we were in a word of honour at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you were in a word of honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm getting all kinds of meaningful glances, so I better double-check what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was trying to signal that you have to turn off your microphone when the witness answers because of the voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm ready. On, off, on, off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say your word of honour, are you referring to the term "besa"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, besa is the word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, besa is something which is very important in your culture, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Besa is something very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I believe there's some kind of expression that goes something like this: The world may shake, the world may split, but never besa. That's how important it is in your culture. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in our culture very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And besa occurs when there is a need for two disputing families to come to an agreement about something. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when that occurs, when besa is given, that requires that various members of the community come together to discuss and iron out the difficulties or the differences that exist between the disputing families. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what you're telling us happened in this situation? And by that I mean the situation between -- are you okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you need some water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't drink water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What happened in the situation between you and the Behluli family, I take it, is that the community came together and you agreed that there would be no more disputes. True?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because we had given each other the word of honour. And then the war started, and we didn't contact each other, we didn't gather together anymore after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you engage in this word of honour, this besa, before you had a fight with them on New Year's Eve in Shtime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after you had given your word of honour, your family, if I'm not mistaken, got in a fight with the people that you had been feuding with after you had given your word of honour. And you were involved in paying them back. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. What did I have to pay back?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, after the word of honour was given there was another fight between your two families. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, without mentioning any names of your family members, as a result of that fight a number of your family members were put in jail. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some fell in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as a matter of fact as you sit here today, right now, this family dispute, the dispute between your two families, continues, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There is no more dispute between us. We are reconciled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken with your son about this matter, about whether or not the two families have reconciled or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Then the war started. As I said, we didn't have anything else with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we're clear about your testimony. My question is: Have you spoken with your son about whether or not the feud between your two families continues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because my son doesn't have any problem anymore with them. We don't have anything to do with them anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day that you were taken from your home, the dispute you were having with this family was going on at that time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did what he had to do. He finished with that and that was it. I don't know what to say anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told us that at that time a couple of items other than a rifle were taken. One was a generator and one, I believe, was your mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The generator that was taken, is that a large generator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a big one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many men it took to carry that generator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the generator was taken, did you see that generator put into one of the cars that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They put it inside our car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They put that in the trunk of the car. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the trunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other thing that you told us they took, I believe, was a mobile phone. True?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they took the mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who you had service with, what company you were working with at that time, sir? And by "working with," I mean what company was giving you the ability to use the mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I don't know that. The brother was working in Germany at the time. Now I don't really know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the brother was working in Germany, once again without mentioning any names, I take it you're talking about your brother, being the brother who was working in Germany. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Because the telephone -- mobile telephone belonged to my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that phone, the phone that you were using, the phone that belonged to your brother was a phone he had lent you that you were using in Kosovo during that time. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. His wife actually had the mobile telephone with her, and then his wife gave it to me and the telephone was with me non-stop after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this gentleman a gentleman who was on the side of the Behlulis or was this gentleman somebody who was, in your opinion, neutral during this dispute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was not taking any sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he said to you that you thought that you would never fall to into his hands, what did that mean to you? What was that referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, actually, what he meant with that, falling in his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was somebody who lived in your village. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was somebody who was aware of the dispute that existed between the two families, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He knew, but he wasn't linked with us or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say he wasn't linked with you, I take it what you mean by that he didn't support your side of this particular dispute. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he didn't have anything to do with this dispute, I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of days ago you met with the Prosecutor in this case, the gentleman who was asking you questions earlier today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time you gave to him for the very first time a description of the man that you have identified as Shala. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the description that you gave him but a couple of days ago, you told Mr. Whiting that this individual, Shala, had a moustache. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I said that I had never -- I hadn't seen Shala, hadn't taken a good look of Shala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you said that you hadn't taken a good look at Shala, you nonetheless just a couple of days ago gave Mr. Whiting a description of who this person looked like. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I told him about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told him that this man was a tall man. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't know -- do you know how tall you are, sir, how many centimetres tall you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't measure myself, to tell you the truth, neither myself nor Shala. Now I can't tell really how tall Shala is. But I know him, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the man that you described as being tall a man who is taller than you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I mentioned it earlier, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask for the same consideration that we dealt with with the previous witness with regard to the issue of height.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no objection. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told Mr. Whiting when you spoke with him that this man Shala was not thin at the time and was well-built. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had to be well-built since he beat me with a heavy stick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a strong man. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. Hadn't he been strong, he wouldn't beat me that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the stick that he beat you with, that was a big stick. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And he beat me a lot and caused me a lot of injuries and left me right there on the ground. He beat me black and blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, how long have you had a television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: TV set, I've had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you obtain your television set after the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, all the time I've had a TV set.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told us that you have seen Haradin Bala on television. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not on TV, but when he beat me, when he used to beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To put it simple in Albanian, simple and plain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To put it simply to you, sir, you've told us that you saw Haradin Bala on television. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Objection. That's actually not as I recall what he said. He said he saw the accused on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, he can correct it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This last one I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be clearer modified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have watched television concerning this matter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For this matter? I didn't watch on TV that -- in that many details. I didn't spend all my time in front of the TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did spend your time in front of the TV, you saw on the television the people who have been accused of crimes regarding this matter. True?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm telling you that this is the person. As for the other persons, I don't know. For this person, I'm sure. I'm telling you, this is the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "this person, this is the one," this is a person you have seen on television. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shala, yes. On TV or whatever, that's what I'm telling you. This is the thing I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times have you seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm -- I don't watch TV that much. I don't stay -- I don't spend that much time in front of the TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is: How many times have you seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every time they would show him, I would see him when I would be there to watch TV; otherwise, I wouldn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More than ten times; would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't quite understand this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen him on television more than ten times? Would that be a fair number of times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lately I haven't seen him. Before, yes, before I've seen him on TV. The thing is, we do not have electricity all the time to watch TV there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him on television, did you see him -- I'm sorry. Let me ask that question again. When you saw him on television, were you with any other members of your family watching television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know his family members, to tell you the truth. I do not know his family members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to your family members, sir. Did you watch television with your brother, without mentioning his name, or your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not have anybody at home. All are abroad and now I can't tell you whether they saw him on TV or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person at Lapusnik by the name I believe of Murrizi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe him for us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was dark-skinned and short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say he was short, I take it that he was shorter than you are. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was shorter than me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any facial hair? A moustache?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what colour was his hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Black colour, black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of his eyes, Murrizi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember anything about him at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Murrizi wear a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Black uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about this man Shala? Do you remember his eyes? Did he have dark eyes with his dark skin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember, but on that day when we went upwards, I remember they would call him "Murrizi," but I never took a good look at him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that you are mistaken in your identification of Haradin Bala as being the person who has done the things that you have testified about here today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why do you think I'm mistaken? I do not think I have got anything wrong here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that it is your watching of television and seeing my client, Haradin Bala, on television that has brought you to the conclusion that he is a person responsible for these things.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the person responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. I was thinking that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- this would be a good moment for a break, on the assumption that you might need a little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, as always, is ahead of the game.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm never confident of that, but I try. We will resume at a quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Could we please be in -- go in private session for the first two questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now in open session, sir, that means no names, please. Would you be good enough to listen to my question very carefully. As they were taking you away, as they were taking your generator, as they were taking your mobile phone, did you think that it might have something to do with the dispute that was going on? Did you think that as it was happening that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. There must have been some links to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: That's all I ask. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I just have a few more questions for you. You identified in this courtroom the man that you knew as Shala in Lapusnik. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you identify Shala in this courtroom because he was the man you knew as Shala in Lapusnik or because you watched television?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that's -- the answer to that question is something for the Chamber to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The reality certainly is. I think we may properly -- if this is put by way of clarification, which I take it to be, that may be a proper subject of questioning, in view of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question because we were interrupted. Witness, is -- did you identify Shala in this courtroom because he was the man you knew as Shala in Lapusnik or because you had watched television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hadn't seen him on television then. First I saw him in Lapusnik and then afterwards I saw him on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is he the man, the man that you identified here in the courtroom here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I've just been signaled to remember to turn off my microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The man that you identified in the courtroom here today, is he the man that you knew as Shala in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you certain about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We're in open session, so I'm going to ask you not to use names. But you have talked about a dispute that your family had with another family. Do you recall talking about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall talking about a dispute that you had and your family had with another family in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We had that dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did that dispute have anything to do with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In what sense did it have something to do with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the person who took me, he worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But your fight, your dispute, was it a dispute -- did you have any dispute with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. You mean my family members?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. You and your family, did you have any dispute or fight with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The dispute with the other people in your village, did that have anything to do with Shala? Did Shala have anything to do with that dispute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was involved in the sense of being a friend of a friend of a friend, because Ramadan's friend is Shala's brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did anybody with the name Qerqiz have anything to do with that dispute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This -- I don't know about Qerqiz. I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And finally, when you were at Lapusnik did anybody talk to you about that dispute that you were having with the other family in your village? And I mean did any of the guards or soldiers talk to you about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody did say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm pleased to be able to tell you that that concludes the questions that you will be asked. The Chamber is grateful that you've come to The Hague to assist us, and we thank you for that. And you will be able shortly to leave the court and return to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you just wait there a moment because the screens will have to be closed. While that is happening, it appears that we are at the end of the witnesses you have available. Is that correct, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We had anticipated that this witness would be longer. My direct, however, was shorter than Mr. Guy-Smith's cross-examination was shorter. So we thought that it would be -- go into tomorrow. We didn't want to bring another witness who would then have to continue after the holiday. So, yes, we do not have any other witnesses for this week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Fortunately the season of the year is such that the Chamber hasn't the spirit to be at all critical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It means now, though, that we must adjourn now until after the vacation. We resume on Thursday, the 13th of January, at 2.15 in the afternoon. I think that the Chamber should express its regret to the three accused that there will be this long disruption in their trial, but you will understand that with a vacation that happens only twice a year, these things are unavoidable. We adjourn until then and we extend to everybody the compliments of the season and we look forward to seeing you in the new year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two matters. One, I had asked you to guard a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I no longer need for you to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am grateful for that. I have it noted for our first day back to ask you. I still have it. I will not have it after today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. The other matter is we wish you all a very happy holiday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of January, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.04 p.m.,
